source_manifest_differences.manifest: Discontinuity of $f$ at a point of its domain, and its classification: removable discontinuity, jump discontinuity and essential discontinuity, equivalently Rudin's discontinuities of the first and of the second kind
source_manifest_differences.source: Discontinuity at a domain point: removable, jump and essential cases, and the first- and second-kind grouping

source_manifest_differences.manifest: A monotone function on an interval has no discontinuity of the second kind: at every point both relevant one-sided limits exist, and an interior point $c$ is a discontinuity exactly when $\lim_{x \to c^{-}} f(x) < \lim_{x \to c^{+}} f(x)$
source_manifest_differences.source: Monotone functions have every relevant finite one-sided limit; interior discontinuities are jumps, with side limits ordered by the direction of monotonicity
